## Step 5 — Findings

```
**Finding:** Missing `<title>` element for the page/document context
**WCAG:** 2.4.2 Title of Page
**Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure
**Severity:** MINOR
**Route to:** Content Author (secondary: Front-End Dev)
**Evidence:** Component source does not render or manage `<title>`; relies on parent framework/page shell
**Fix:** Ensure the parent page layout or routing layer injects a unique, descriptive `<title>` matching the product name and site context. [Human verification required — cannot be confirmed from component source]
```

```
**Finding:** Missing `lang` attribute on root `<html>` element
**WCAG:** 3.1.1 Language of Page
**Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure
**Severity:** MINOR
**Route to:** Content Author (secondary: Front-End Dev)
**Evidence:** Component source does not render or manage `<html lang>`; relies on parent framework/page shell
**Fix:** Ensure the root document declares `lang="en"` (or appropriate locale). [Human verification required — cannot be confirmed from component source]
```

```
**Finding:** Breadcrumb list uses `<ol>` instead of `<ul>`
**WCAG:** 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (APG guidance)
**Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure
**Severity:** ENHANCEMENT
**Route to:** UX Design (secondary: Front-End Dev)
**Evidence:** `references/perspectives.md` checklist / APG pattern for breadcrumbs recommends `<ul>` as breadcrumbs represent a list of links, not a numbered sequence.
**Fix:** Replace `<ol className="breadcrumb">` with `<ul className="breadcrumb">`. Screen readers will announce it as an unordered list, aligning with assistive technology expectations.
```
